mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS declines (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and investor confidence, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (HOUST rising and UNRATE falling) does not produce positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of instances (or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenue growth slows.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, RSAFS decline does not lead to negative 20-day forward returns (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% (or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening residential demand and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants anticipate improved corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 102, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output, reducing corporate profitability and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 102 (or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the federal funds rate increases borrowing costs and reduces liquidity, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, a rise in FEDFUNDS does not lead to negative 20-day forward returns (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
